chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas related to me that al-Hasan ibn Yusuf said on the authority of 'Abd al-Salam, on the authority of 'Ammar ibn Abu al-Yaqzan, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will come on the Day of Judgment holding the waistband of his Lord, and we will be holding the waistband of our Prophet, and our Shi'ites will be holding our waistband. So we and our Shi'ites are the Party of Allah, and the Party of Allah are the triumphant ones. By Allah, we do not claim that it is the waistband of the garment, but rather it is greater than that. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will come holding the religion of Allah, and we will come holding the religion of our Prophet, and our Shi'ites will come holding our religion.

key_terms.إِزَار: Garment or loincloth, used here as a literal contrast to the spiritual 'waistband'
key_terms.الدِّين: Religion or way of life, here signifying the specific teachings and authority of the Prophet and Imams
key_terms.حُجْزَة: Waistband or girdle, symbolizing authority and adherence
key_terms.حِزْبُ اللَّهِ: The Party of God, referring to the Shi'ites as the victorious group

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of holding the 'waistband' (hujzah) on the Day of Judgment in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies that the 'waistband' (hujzah) is not merely a physical garment but a metaphor for holding fast to the essence of religion (din), establishing a chain of spiritual authority from God to the Prophet, then to the Imams, and finally to the Shi'ites. This hadith underscores the Shia doctrine of *wilayah* as the defining characteristic of the *Hizb Allah* (Party of God), linking their eschatological success directly to their adherence to the Imams' teachings. The narration serves as a theological foundation for the concept of *shi'a* as a distinct, victorious community bound by this divine connection.
